content.user_title: Design Game Assets, Cutscenes, and Web Showcases
content.value_statement: Character art, cinematics, and browser demos can drift apart when teams plan them separately. Use shared design briefs, camera prompts, and layout examples to keep them consistent.
actual_capabilities: Define fixed facial features, clothing, and colors for front, three-quarter, side, and rear character views.
Specify frames and poses for idle, run, attack, and hit reaction sprite cycles.
Structure cutscene prompts around starting framing, camera rig, motion, tracking target, environmental effects, and ending framing.
Draft cover art prompts and Tailwind card layouts with focal subjects, titles, and badges.
Outline responsive Canvas and WebGL demo grids with browser audio cues and a story route into gameplay.
limitations: The skill supplies prompts and specifications, not a built-in image or video renderer.
The game references contain blueprints, not eight runnable games.
Frontend examples require integration and testing with your own game builds and assets.
Visual consistency and click-through rates are not guaranteed.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Character Handoff
use_cases.description: Document fixed costume details and four views so modelers and sprite artists can work from the same brief.

use_cases.title: Plan the Transition Into Gameplay
use_cases.description: Define how a cutscene frames its subject and ends at the playable camera view.

use_cases.title: Organize Browser Game Demos
use_cases.description: Plan responsive cards, launch routes, and sound controls for a mix of 2D and 3D demos.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Character Turnaround
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a turnaround prompt for [character]. Keep the face, clothing, colors, and proportions fixed across front, three-quarter, side, and rear views.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Prepare an art brief for a single character.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a Showcase Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cover art prompt for [game] using [main subject] as the focal point. Suggest a title placement and badge that stay legible at 320 pixels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Prepare a thumbnail for a game library.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Cutscene Camera
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a cutscene for [scene] that ends at [gameplay view]. Specify the starting frame, camera rig, speed, tracking target, environmental effects, and final frame.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Prepare a shot brief for a trailer or playable sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Browser Game Showcase
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a responsive showcase for [demo list]. Define card sizes, local launch routes, and an opt-in audio control. Add a story transition into [featured demo] and a mobile test checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Coordinate the site layout, launch flow, and testing for several games.

output_examples.input: Plan four views and two sprite cycles for a mechanic in a teal jacket.
output: Keep the teal jacket, silver zipper, and short black hair identical in all four views.
Show the mechanic from the front, three-quarter angle, side, and rear under the same lighting.
Use four frames for a breathing idle and six for a run cycle.

output_examples.input: Draft a race intro that ends in the playable chase view.
output: Open low behind the rear wheels. Use a virtual chase rig that accelerates into the first bend.
Track the rear lights as wet pavement reflects the track signs.
Ease upward into the playable chase view before the countdown begins.

output_examples.input: Plan a front page for one racing demo and two Canvas puzzle games.
output: Give the racing demo a wide card on desktop and place all three cards in one column on mobile.
Use a separate launch route for each demo and keep sound off until the user enables it.
Check that the titles remain readable at 320 pixels and each launch button works with a keyboard.

best_practices: Reuse the same character identity brief for each view and action pose.
Choose the playable camera angle before writing the final cutscene frame.
Test generated layouts on mobile and desktop with the actual demo builds.
anti_patterns: Changing identifying features between turnaround views.
Treating a cutscene prompt as a rendered video or working camera animation.
Presenting a showcase card or blueprint as a tested playable game.

faq.question: What does the skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces text briefs, generation prompts, sprite specifications, and frontend examples.

faq.question: Can it render images or videos by itself?
faq.answer: No. Rendering requires an image or video tool that can use the prompts.

faq.question: Can I use only the cutscene workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. Describe the scene and the gameplay view you want the cutscene to end on.

faq.question: Does it include playable games?
faq.answer: It includes game blueprints and sample components. Supply or build the playable demos separately.

faq.question: Can the same showcase include 2D and 3D games?
faq.answer: Yes. The layout can group HTML5 Canvas and WebGL demos with separate launch routes.

faq.question: Does the card guidance guarantee more clicks?
faq.answer: No. It provides composition and readability guidance. Test variants with your audience to measure results.
